statements.text: The Readiness tab is the command page: every question and every blocking item is a table row with a count and a link that opens the item where it lives, and what settles it is stated beside it in plain words; the viewer is read-only and renders no command text.

The viewer exposes trace, impact and coverage for a selected node through GET routes computed from the current tree, and renders a coverage summary and a trace matrix, so a reader sees how far the chain reaches without the CLI.

The command page works for a human with no agent in the loop, stays embed-safe under embed=1 and both themes, adds no dependency, never writes to rcf/manifest.json, and leaves the computeReadiness signature unchanged.

Issue 333 items 1 and 2 (reporter WESPA de-flake pass AI-2007, filed 2026-10-08 against 0.32.4): the live-view server watcher now queues exactly one trailing rewalk when a change arrives mid-rewalk (coalesce, never drop) and fatal watcher and walker exceptions surface to stderr regardless of --verbose. Build amendment under src/server/index.js (startServer carries a new logError sink and an injectable renderImpl seam for tests) and src/cli/view.js (wires logError unconditionally). Chatty per-event lines (sse write failures) remain gated on --verbose. Item 3 (diffed tree updates) scheduled for 0.33.0.

Issue 336 (reporter Dex, filed 2026-10-08 against 0.32.5): the live-view server watcher goes blind to a file after a rename-save on Linux (recursive fs.watch reports the first rename, then never again for that path). Fix: on a rename event the watch primitive now re-arms the affected base (close and reopen the fs.watch handle), one re-arm per debounce window. src/watch/index.js carries a new fsWatchImpl seam for deterministic cross-platform tests; no dependency added; no AC under the viewer stories binds the rename-blind behaviour so this is recorded as a build amendment. Rides 0.33.0.

A product declares at intake whether its UI is none, light or central; a light or central product carries a tool-minted journey record (every entry, exit, interruption and return path, each step naming its screen) answering the interruption catalogue, a central product adds a wireframe file per step reviewed under a content hash, and DEFINE refuses to open on a light or central product whose discovery is not complete.

The gate is not tight: wireframe richness is better discovery input and never mandated input, only a central product is refused for a missing wireframe, the interruption check is answered rather than drawn, existing trees are grandfathered with no rollout mechanism, D0 is never acknowledgeable, journey steps are never a traceability node, and the record is written only by the tool.

Verification of a build spec happens in the Test stage, before merge, by a verifier hand that is not the builder, through the real entry point on the preview or version host; Finalise after merge is an administrative step that writes verified from that evidence and spawns no agent.
No later spec on a product enters Build until every merged spec on it is verified, enforced by the tool rather than by a brief.
A mechanical check reads a pull request's commits and fails when a hand touches tests, criteria or production code outside its lane, printing one line a gate can quote.
URL-verifiable acceptance criteria verify deterministically from a per-AC probe catalog, so a dispatched worker can verify without spawning an agent.
